stories.title: You Can See Everything in Elizabeth Holmes’s unblinking eyes. Or can you? | Jason Okundaye
stories.summary: The idea that seeing is believing is turned on its head in this documentary about the inscrutable Theranos founder, a world-class liar who may just be completely unreadable Elizabeth Holmes doesn’t believe that she’s ever told a lie. She “knows” that she hasn’t committed any crime. And she has no reason to deceive you. While speaking, she is gazing at her interviewer, Nathan Fielder, with those enormous, blue, vacant, unsettling, unblinking eyes. She doesn’t break eye contact. This is You Can See Everything, Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary, which, at her invitation, follows Holmes and her husband, Billy Evans, at their home in San Diego in the weeks up to her surrender to custody at federal prison. Holmes is the disgraced tech ex-billionaire whose startup Theranos claimed the ability to run hundreds of comprehensive blood tests from a single pinprick of blood. This false claim posed “immediate jeopardy” to the health of thousands of patients and defrauded investors of more than $700m. Continue reading...

stories.summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.2a0 I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday . Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent , so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools. Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: Download the video (MP4) I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time as a chart" - where typing "#stats" opens a table search box. It shows me a chart inline in the chat, and when I click "Open in the chart builder" it opens the chart in a panel along with the table page. I use the table page to switch to a chart of "datasette", then when I ask the agent "what does the chart show?" it notices that I changed the content in the panel and describes the new Datasette chart to me. stories.title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab's AI science benchmark
GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
stories.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API. It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model. I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because llm-zai doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up. Here are pelicans for GLM-5.4 on low, high, and max. This is the max one: I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4. It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look. I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark. Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , llm , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , llm-release , ai-in-china , glm
